'''Diane Grob Schmidt''' (born November 1945) is an American [[chemist]], who was the executive at [[Procter & Gamble|Procter & Gamble Co.]] in [[Cincinnati, Ohio]], from 1981 to 2014.<ref name=ChemBond/><ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-01-05 |title=Diane Schmidt {{!}} Department of Chemistry |url=https://chem.utk.edu/people/diane-schmidt/ |access-date=2022-03-16 |language=en-US}}</ref>  In 2015, she served as president of the [[American Chemical Society]] (ACS).<ref name=Coyle>{{cite news|last1=Coyle|first1=Joan|title=Diane Grob Schmidt elected 2015 president of world's largest scientific society|url=http://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/pressroom/newsreleases/2013/december/diane-grob-schmidt-elected-2015-president-of-worlds-largest-scientific-society.html|access-date=9 December 2015|work=ACS Chemistry for Life|date=December 18, 2013}}</ref> As of 2022, she was serving as the chair of the board of visitors for the department of chemistry at the [[University of Tennessee, Knoxville]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Diane Schmidt Chair, Board of Visitors |url=https://chem.utk.edu/people/diane-schmidt/ |website=University of Tennessee, Knoxville Department of Chemistry |access-date=16 March 2022}}</ref>

==Education==
Diane Grob Schmidt grew up in [[Lorain, Ohio]], and [[Chattanooga, Tennessee]].<ref name=ChemBond/> She graduated from Red Bank High School in the class of 1963.  She received her A.B. from the [[University of Tennessee at Chattanooga]] in 1967,<ref name=Chattanooga>{{cite news|title=UTC alumna becomes 2015 president of world's largest scientific society|url=http://blog.utc.edu/news/2015/01/utc-alumna-becomes-2015-president-worlds-largest-scientific-society/|access-date=9 December 2015|work=UTC News|agency=University of Tennessee Chattanooga|date=January 23, 2015}}</ref> her  M.S. from the [[University of Tennessee]], [[Knoxville, Tennessee|Knoxville]], and her Ph.D. in organic chemistry from the [[University of Cincinnati]] in 1981.<ref name=ChemBond/>

==Career==
Diane Grob Schmidt joined [[Procter & Gamble|Procter & Gamble Co.]] in [[Cincinnati, Ohio]], in 1981 and retired in 2014.<ref name=ChemBond/>  She was appointed as a senior scientist from 1992 to 1997 and as section head beginning in 1997.<ref name=CAEN2013/> As a section head, she was responsible for safety and regulatory affairs.<ref name=Rubber>{{cite journal|title=ACS president to deliver keynote at Elastomer Conference|journal=Rubber & Plastics News Report|date=July 27, 2015|url=http://www.rubbernews.com/article/20150727/NEWS/150729970?template=printart|access-date=9 December 2015}}</ref> She has also been an adjunct professor in the department of chemistry in the University of Cincinnati.<ref name=Chattanooga/>

Diane Grob Schmidt holds a number of patents, including a patent for [[Pert Plus]] shampoo and conditioner formula. She led the team of scientists at Procter & Gamble who developed Pert Plus, the first combined shampoo and conditioner.<ref name=TenThings>{{cite news|title=Ten Things You Didn't Know about UTC|url=http://alumnus.tennessee.edu/2011/09/ten-things-you-didnt-know-about-utc/|access-date=9 December 2015|work=Tennessee Alumnus|date=6 September 2011}}</ref>

She has served on the editorial boards of the ''Journal of the Society of Cosmetic Chemists'' and the ''Journal of Chemical Health & Safety''.<ref name=McMicken>{{cite web|title=McMicken College of Arts and Sciences Alumni and Faculty Members Honored for Achievements|url=http://www.uc.edu/news/NR.aspx?id=19709|website=McMicken College of Arts and Sciences|access-date=9 December 2015}}</ref>

Diane Grob Schmidt is a member of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS) and of the [[American Industrial Hygiene Association]].<ref name=CAEN2013/>  She has been a member of the American Chemical Society (ACS) since 1968 and has held a wide variety of positions whose scope has included chemical health and safety, and chemistry & the law.<ref name=CAEN2013>{{cite journal|title=For President-Elect: Diane Grob Schmidt|journal=Chemical & Engineering News|date=September 16, 2013|volume=91|issue=37|pages=38–40|url=http://cen.acs.org/articles/91/i37/President-Elect-Diane-Grob-Schmidt.html|access-date=9 December 2015}}</ref>  These included three consecutive terms on the board of directors.<ref name=Rubber/> In 2015, she became president of the [[American Chemical Society]] (ACS).<ref name=Coyle>{{cite news|last1=Coyle|first1=Joan|title=Diane Grob Schmidt elected 2015 president of world's largest scientific society|url=http://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/pressroom/newsreleases/2013/december/diane-grob-schmidt-elected-2015-president-of-worlds-largest-scientific-society.html|access-date=9 December 2015|work=ACS Chemistry for Life|date=December 18, 2013}}</ref> Her presidential theme was “Inspiring and Innovating for Tomorrow.”<ref name=ChemBond>{{cite journal|last1=Grob Schmidt|first1=Diane|title=You And ACS: Relevant, Energized, Committed|journal=Chembond|date=2015|volume=Spring|pages=10–12|url=http://www.artsci.uc.edu/content/dam/artsci/departments/chemistry/Docs/ChemBond2015.pdf|access-date=9 December 2015}}</ref> She co-edited 5 books while in the Presidential succession and wrote introductions and chapters in each.

==Awards and honors==
* 2016, Fellow, National Academy of Inventors<ref name=NAI>{{cite web|title= Fellows|url=https://academyofinventors.org/search-fellows|website=NAI Fellows|access-date=30 August 2024}}</ref> 
* 2016, Fellow, American Association for the Advancement of Science<ref name=Science>{{cite web|title=2016 Fellows|url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/2016|website=AAAS|access-date=30 August 2024}}</ref>
* 2014, Distinguished Alumna of the University of Cincinnati<ref name=Cincinnati>{{cite web|title=Alumni Recipients|url=http://www.artsci.uc.edu/alumni-friends/distinguished-alumni-awards/alumni-recipients.html|website=University of Cincinnati|access-date=9 December 2015}}</ref>
* 2012, Henry A. Hill Award, ACS Division of Professional Relations<ref name=Hill>{{cite news|title=Chemistry Board of Visitors Chair Received The Henry Hill Award from ACS|url=https://www.chem.utk.edu/news/chemistry-board-visitors-chair-received-henry-hill-award-acs|access-date=9 December 2015|work=The University of Tennessee Knoxville|date=April 10, 2012}}</ref>
* 2011,  Fellow, American Chemical Society<ref name=ACS2011>{{cite news|title=2011 ACS Fellows|url=http://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/fellows/list-of-2011-acs-fellows.html|access-date=9 December 2015|work=ACS Chemistry for Life}}</ref>
* 2004, Fellow, ACS Chemical Health & Safety Division<ref name=CAEN2013/>
* 1995, Distinguished Alumna, from the University of Tennessee, Chattanooga<ref name=Chattanooga/> 
* 1994, Distinguished Scientist of Cincinnati, from the Engineers and Scientists of Cincinnati (first woman so honored)<ref name=CAEN2013/>
* [[Sigma Xi]] (life member)
* [[Iota Sigma Pi]] (life member)
